ko.title: [마케팅 101 #15] 마지막 수업: 한 학기 내용을 한 페이지에 담기

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > 마케팅 계획이란 우리가 어디에 있는지, 누구를 위한 것인지, 무엇을 제공할 것인지, 비용은 얼마인지, 그리고 그것이 효과가 있었는지 어떻게 알 수 있는지에 대한 다섯 가지 솔직한 답변을 모두가 볼 수 있는 곳에 적어둔 것입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: 당신이 들어본 모든 마케팅 아이디어는 하나의 질문에 답하려고 합니다: **낯선 사람이 왜 다른 사람 대신 당신에게 돈을 지불할까요?**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: 마케팅 계획은 그 질문에 대해 소리 내어 답하도록 강제하는 문서입니다.

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: 대부분은 동일한 뼈대를 따르며, 각 뼈대는 마케터들이 한 학기 내내 공부하는 내용과 대응됩니다:

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: 상황 분석 — 우리는 정말 어디에 있는가?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: 일반적인 약어는 **5C**입니다: Company(우리가 실제로 잘하는 것), Customers(누가, 왜 구매하는가), Competitors(누가 이 문제를 해결하는가), Collaborators(유통업체, 소매업체, 대행사), 그리고 Context(경제, 규제, 기술, 문화).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: 많은 팀이 이를 SWOT(강점, 약점, 기회, 위협)으로 압축하지만, SWOT은 연구의 요약일 뿐 연구를 대체할 수는 없습니다.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: 상황 분석에 숫자가 없다면, 그것은 무드 보드일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: 목표 — 승리란 어떤 모습인가?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: "인지도 향상"은 목표가 아니라 바람입니다.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: 목표에는 숫자, 지표, 마감 기한이 있어야 합니다: *4분기까지 재구매율을 22%에서 30%로 높인다.* 모호한 목표는 마케팅 예산이 조용히 사라지는 원인입니다.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: 세분화, 타겟팅, 포지셔닝(STP) — 이것은 누구를 위한 것인가?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: 시장을 다르게 행동하는 그룹으로 나누고(세분화), 실제로 이길 수 있고 수익성 있게 서비스할 수 있는 그룹을 선택한 다음(타겟팅), 그들의 머릿속에 각인시키고 싶은 하나의 아이디어를 결정하세요(포지셔닝).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: 포지셔닝은 무엇이 되지 않을 것인가에 대한 선택입니다.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: 프리미엄이면서 저렴하고, 가장 빠르면서 가장 건강한 브랜드는 그 무엇도 아닙니다.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: 마케팅 믹스 — 우리는 실제로 무엇을 할 것인가?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: 고전적인 **4P**: Product(무엇이며, 무엇을 약속하는가), Price(비용은 얼마이며 무엇을 암시하는가), Place(사람들이 어디서 어떻게 얻을 수 있는가), Promotion(그들이 어떻게 알게 되는가).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: 서비스업은 종종 세 가지 P를 더 추가합니다 — People(사람), Process(과정), Physical evidence(물리적 증거) — 이발이나 치과 진료에서는 경험 자체가 곧 제품이기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: 좋은 계획의 시험대는 일관성입니다: 네 가지 P는 모두 같은 이야기를 하고 있어야 합니다.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: 예산 및 통제 — 비용은 얼마이며, 효과가 있었는지 어떻게 알 수 있는가?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: 돈, 일정, 담당자, 그리고 확인할 지표들입니다.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: 통제 단계는 사람들이 건너뛰는 부분이지만, 마케팅을 비용 센터에서 규율로 바꾸는 핵심 단계입니다.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: 계획은 가설입니다.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: 통제는 실험입니다.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: 이것이 한 학기 전체의 내용입니다: 상황을 조사하고, 고객을 선택하고, 일관된 제안을 만들고, 의도적으로 지출하고, 정직하게 측정하십시오.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상에서의 적용

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: 당신이 오스틴의 작은 커피 브랜드인 **Barton Springs Cold Brew**를 운영한다고 가정해 봅시다.

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: 전국적으로 온라인 판매를 하고 있으며, 텍사스 중부의 12개 식료품점 매대에 제품이 놓여 있습니다.

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: 지난 분기 매출은 4만 달러였습니다.

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: 6만 달러를 원합니다.

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: 여기 한 페이지짜리 계획이 있습니다.

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **상황:** 콜드브루 시장은 붐비고, 대형 전국 브랜드들이 식료품 매대를 장악하고 있습니다.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: 하지만 재구매 고객들은 한 가지를 극찬합니다 — 산도가 낮아서 위장이 예민한 사람들도 블랙으로 마실 수 있다는 점입니다.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: 경쟁사들은 "강렬함"과 "고카페인"을 외치고 있습니다.

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: 아무도 "부드러움"을 외치지 않습니다.

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **목표:** 12월 31일까지 분기 매출을 4만 달러에서 6만 달러로 성장시키고, 최소 40%는 재구매 고객으로부터 발생하게 한다.

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** 대학생 에너지 음료 수요층은 건너뜁니다 — 그것은 당신이 질 수밖에 없는 가격 전쟁입니다.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: 커피가 위장을 불편하게 해서 커피를 줄인 텍사스 대도시의 30~55세 매일 커피를 마시는 사람들을 타겟팅합니다.

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: 포지셔닝은 *매일 아침 후회 없이 마실 수 있는 콜드브루*로 합니다.

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **마케팅 믹스:** 제품 — 뒷면에 숨기지 말고 앞면 라벨에 "저산도, 위장에 부드러움"을 넣습니다.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: 가격 — 4팩 구독 상품을 32달러로 유지합니다; 할인은 프리미엄이라는 주장을 약화시킬 것입니다.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: 유통 — 감당할 수 없는 전국 유통을 쫓기보다 건강을 생각하는 지역의 H-E-B 매장에 집중합니다.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: 프로모션 — 인스타그램의 고객 후기와 오스틴의 두 러닝 클럽과의 파트너십을 활용합니다.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **예산 및 통제:** 분기당 9,000달러.

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: 그리고 모든 것을 결정하는 숫자는 이것입니다:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: 신규 고객에게 첫 판매를 할 때 **약 40센트의 손해**를 봅니다. 이것이 자동으로 실패는 아닙니다 — 그들이 다시 돌아오지 않을 때만 실패입니다.

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: 연평균 2.5회 주문 시, 평생 기여도는 대략 `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`이며, 획득 비용 18달러 대비 약 2.4 대 1입니다.

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: 이 계획은 유지율이 유지될 때만 작동합니다.

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: 따라서 매주 지켜봐야 할 지표는 노출수나 좋아요가 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: 바로 재구매율입니다.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: 이것이 마케팅 계획이 실제로 하는 일입니다: 당신이 조용히 의존하고 있던 가정을 밖으로 끌어내어 테스트할 수 있게 만드는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. 마케팅 계획은 상황, 목표, STP, 마케팅 믹스, 예산 및 통제라는 사슬이며, 어디든 약한 고리가 있으면 전체가 무너집니다.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. 포지셔닝은 무엇이 되지 않을지 결정하는 것이며, 4P는 그 하나의 선택을 강화해야 합니다.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. 계획이 의존하는 숫자를 적고 측정하십시오 — 테스트되지 않은 계획은 예산이 포함된 의견일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a properly written marketing objective?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 다음 중 올바르게 작성된 마케팅 목표는 무엇입니까?

segments.src: ① Become the most loved coffee brand in Texas
segments.tr: ① 텍사스에서 가장 사랑받는 커피 브랜드가 되기

segments.src: ② Increase brand awareness significantly
segments.tr: ② 브랜드 인지도를 크게 높이기

segments.src: ③ Raise repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by December 31
segments.tr: ③ 12월 31일까지 재구매율을 22%에서 30%로 높이기

segments.src: ④ Beat our competitors
segments.tr: ④ 경쟁사 이기기

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) If a company's customer acquisition cost is higher than the contribution margin on a single order, the marketing plan is definitely losing money.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 기업의 고객 획득 비용이 단일 주문의 공헌 이익보다 높다면, 그 마케팅 계획은 확실히 돈을 잃고 있는 것이다.

segments.src: **Q3.** A brand positions itself as "affordable everyday value," then launches in luxury department stores at a premium price.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 한 브랜드가 "합리적인 일상 가치"로 포지셔닝한 후, 고급 백화점에 프리미엄 가격으로 런칭했습니다.

segments.src: Which principle does this violate?
segments.tr: 어떤 원칙을 위반했습니까?

segments.src: ① Segmentation must come before targeting
segments.tr: ① 세분화는 타겟팅보다 먼저 이루어져야 한다

segments.src: ② The elements of the marketing mix must be consistent with the positioning
segments.tr: ② 마케팅 믹스의 요소들은 포지셔닝과 일관되어야 한다

segments.src: ③ Objectives must be measurable
segments.tr: ③ 목표는 측정 가능해야 한다

segments.src: ④ The situation analysis must include competitors
segments.tr: ④ 상황 분석에는 경쟁자가 포함되어야 한다

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **마케팅 계획(Marketing plan)** — 상황, 목표, 타겟 고객, 마케팅 활동, 예산, 그리고 결과를 판단하는 데 사용되는 지표를 명시한 서면 문서.

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5C** — 상황 분석 체크리스트: Company(회사), Customers(고객), Competitors(경쟁사), Collaborators(협력사), Context(환경).

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — 세분화(Segmentation), 타겟팅(Targeting), 포지셔닝(Positioning): 시장을 나누고, 누구에게 서비스할지 선택하며, 그들의 마음속에 각인시키고 싶은 아이디어를 정의하는 것.

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **마케팅 믹스(4P)** — 제품(Product), 가격(Price), 유통(Place), 촉진(Promotion); 기업이 포지셔닝을 실현하기 위해 사용하는 통제 가능한 수단.

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC와 LTV** — 고객 획득 비용(Customer acquisition cost) 대 고객이 창출하는 평생 기여도(Lifetime contribution); 이 둘의 비율은 성장이 지속 가능한지 아니면 단순히 비용이 많이 드는지를 알려줍니다.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 — ③.
segments.tr: *정답: Q1 — ③.

segments.src: It names a metric, a starting point, a target, and a deadline; the others are aspirations without a way to check them.
segments.tr: 지표, 시작점, 목표, 마감 기한을 명시하고 있습니다; 나머지는 확인할 방법이 없는 열망일 뿐입니다.

segments.src: Q2 — X.
segments.tr: Q2 — X.

segments.src: It's a warning sign, not a verdict.
segments.tr: 그것은 경고 신호이지, 판결이 아닙니다.

segments.src: If customers buy repeatedly, lifetime contribution can comfortably exceed acquisition cost, which is exactly the Barton Springs case — but the plan then lives or dies on retention.
segments.tr: 고객이 반복적으로 구매한다면 평생 기여도가 획득 비용을 충분히 초과할 수 있으며, 이것이 바로 Barton Springs의 사례입니다. 하지만 이 경우 계획은 유지율에 성패가 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: Q3 — ②.
segments.tr: Q3 — ②.

segments.src: The positioning claim and the price/place decisions contradict each other, so customers get no clear story about what the brand is.*
segments.tr: 포지셔닝 주장과 가격/유통 결정이 서로 모순되므로, 고객은 브랜드가 무엇인지에 대해 명확한 이야기를 얻지 못합니다.*

zh.title: [Marketing 101 #15] 最终课：把整学期浓缩在一页纸上

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > 营销计划其实就是五个诚实的回答——我们在哪里、我们面向谁、我们提供什么、成本是多少，以及我们如何知道它是否奏效——把这些写下来，让所有人都能看到。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: 你听过的每一个营销创意都在试图回答一个问题：**为什么陌生人要把钱给你，而不是给别人？**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: 营销计划是一份逼迫你大声回答这个问题的文档。

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: 它们大多数遵循相同的骨架，每根骨架都对应着营销人员整学期学习的内容：

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: 情境分析——我们究竟在哪里？**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: 常见的简写是 **5C**：公司（我们真正擅长什么）、客户（谁在买以及为什么买）、竞争对手（还有谁在解决这个问题）、合作方（分销商、零售商、机构）以及环境（经济、监管、技术、文化）。

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: 许多团队将此压缩为 SWOT（优势、劣势、机会、威胁），但 SWOT 是研究的总结，而不是研究的替代品。

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: 如果你的情境分析里没有数字，它就只是一块情绪板。

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: 目标——获胜是什么样子的？**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: “提高知名度”不是目标；那是个愿望。

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: 一个目标必须包含数字、指标和截止日期：*在第四季度之前，将重复购买率从 22% 提高到 30%。* 模糊的目标正是营销预算悄然消失的原因。

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: 细分、目标、定位（STP）——这是为谁准备的？**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: 把市场分成行为不同的群体（细分），挑选出你能真正赢得并有利可图地服务的群体（目标），然后确定你想在他们心中占据的那一个核心概念（定位）。

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: 定位是一种关于你将*不*做什么的选择。

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: 一个既高端、又便宜、最快且最健康的品牌，其实什么都不是。

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: 营销组合——我们实际上要做什么？**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: 经典的 **4P**：产品（它是什么、它承诺什么）、价格（它花费多少以及这释放了什么信号）、地点（人们在哪里以及如何获取它）、促销（他们如何听说它）。

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: 服务通常会增加另外三个 P——人员、过程、有形展示——因为在理发或看牙医的过程中，体验*就是*产品。

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: 检验一个好计划的标准是连贯性：这四个 P 应该都在讲述同一个故事。

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: 预算与控制——它要花多少钱，我们如何知道它成功了？**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: 资金、时间表、负责人以及你要检查的指标。

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: 控制步骤是人们经常跳过的一个环节，正是它把营销从一个成本中心变成了一门学科。

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: 计划是假设。

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: 控制是实验。

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: 这就是整个学期的内容：研究情境、选择客户、构建连贯的报价、刻意花费并诚实衡量。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: 假设你经营 **Barton Springs Cold Brew**，这是奥斯汀的一个小型咖啡品牌。

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: 你在全网销售，并且在得克萨斯州中部的十几家杂货店货架上都有售。

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: 上个季度你的营业额达到了 40,000 美元。

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: 你希望达到 60,000 美元。

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: 这就是一页纸上的计划。

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **情境：** 冷萃咖啡竞争激烈，大型国家品牌占领了杂货店的货架。

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: 但你的回头客对一件事赞不绝口——它低酸，胃敏感的人可以黑咖饮用。

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: 竞争对手在大喊“浓郁”和“额外咖啡因”。

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: 没有人喊“温和”。

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **目标：** 在 12 月 31 日之前，将季度收入从 4 万美元提升至 6 万美元，其中至少 40% 来自回头客。

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP：** 跳过大学生能量追求者——那是一场你会输掉的价格战。

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: 目标锁定德州大都市区 30-55 岁、因胃部不适而减少喝咖啡的日常咖啡饮用者。

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: 定位为*你可以每天早晨饮用而不会后悔的冷萃咖啡*。

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **营销组合：** 产品——将“低酸、对肠胃温和”写在正面标签上，而不是埋在背面。

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: 价格——4 包订阅装保持在 32 美元；打折会削弱高端宣称。

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: 地点——加倍深耕注重健康的邮政编码内的 H-E-B 门店，而不是去追求你无法服务的全国分销。

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: 促销——Instagram 上的客户证言，以及与两个奥斯汀跑步俱乐部的合作。

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **预算与控制：** 本季度 9,000 美元。

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: 这里是决定一切的数字：

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: 你对新客户的第一笔销售**大约亏损 40 美分。**这不一定自动意味着失败——只有当他们再也不回来时，才是失败。

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: 按平均每年 2.5 笔订单计算，生命周期贡献约为 `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`，获客成本为 18 美元——比例约为 2.4 比 1。

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: 该计划*只有*在留存率保持住的情况下才能奏效。

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: 因此，你每周关注的指标不是曝光量或点赞数。

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: 而是二次购买率。

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: 这就是营销计划真正起到的作用：它将你默默依赖的假设拖到阳光下，供你进行测试。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. 营销计划是一个链条——情境、目标、STP、营销组合、预算与控制——其中任何一个环节薄弱都会破坏整体。

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. 定位意味着决定你不会成为什么；4P 应该共同强化这单一的选择。

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. 写下你的计划所依赖的数字，然后去衡量它——一个未经测试的计划只是一个带预算的观点。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自我测验

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a properly written marketing objective?
segments.tr: **Q1.** 以下哪一项是正确编写的营销目标？

segments.src: ① Become the most loved coffee brand in Texas
segments.tr: ① 成为得克萨斯州最受喜爱的咖啡品牌

segments.src: ② Increase brand awareness significantly
segments.tr: ② 显著提高品牌知名度

segments.src: ③ Raise repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by December 31
segments.tr: ③ 在 12 月 31 日之前将重复购买率从 22% 提高到 30%

segments.src: ④ Beat our competitors
segments.tr: ④ 击败我们的竞争对手

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) If a company's customer acquisition cost is higher than the contribution margin on a single order, the marketing plan is definitely losing money.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 如果公司的客户获取成本高于单笔订单的边际贡献，那么该营销计划肯定在亏钱。

segments.src: **Q3.** A brand positions itself as "affordable everyday value," then launches in luxury department stores at a premium price.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 一个品牌将自己定位为“价格亲民的日常价值”，然后以高端价格在奢侈品百货公司推出。

segments.src: Which principle does this violate?
segments.tr: 这违背了哪个原则？

segments.src: ① Segmentation must come before targeting
segments.tr: ① 细分必须在定位之前

segments.src: ② The elements of the marketing mix must be consistent with the positioning
segments.tr: ② 营销组合的元素必须与定位保持一致

segments.src: ③ Objectives must be measurable
segments.tr: ③ 目标必须是可衡量的

segments.src: ④ The situation analysis must include competitors
segments.tr: ④ 情境分析必须包括竞争对手

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **营销计划** — 详细阐述情境、目标、目标客户、营销行动、预算以及用于评估结果的指标的书面文件。

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5C** — 情境分析检查清单：公司（Company）、客户（Customers）、竞争对手（Competitors）、合作方（Collaborators）、环境（Context）。

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — 细分、目标、定位：划分市场、选择服务对象，并在他们心中定义你想要拥有的概念。

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **营销组合（4P）** — 产品、价格、地点、促销；公司用来兑现其定位的可控杠杆。

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC 与 LTV** — 获客成本与客户产生的生命周期贡献的对比；两者之间的比率告诉你增长是可持续的还是仅仅成本高昂。

segments.tr: *答案：Q1 — ③。

segments.src: It names a metric, a starting point, a target, and a deadline; the others are aspirations without a way to check them.
segments.tr: 它指出了指标、起点、目标和截止日期；其他的则是没有检验方法的愿望。

segments.src: Q2 — X.
segments.tr: Q2 — X。

segments.src: It's a warning sign, not a verdict.
segments.tr: 这是一个警告信号，而不是定论。

segments.src: If customers buy repeatedly, lifetime contribution can comfortably exceed acquisition cost, which is exactly the Barton Springs case — but the plan then lives or dies on retention.
segments.tr: 如果客户重复购买，生命周期贡献可以轻松超过获客成本，这正是 Barton Springs 的案例——但该计划的成败取决于留存率。

segments.tr: एक उद्देश्य में एक संख्या, एक मीट्रिक और एक समय सीमा होती है: *चौथी तिमाही तक बार-बार खरीदारी की दर 22% से बढ़ाकर 30% करना।* अस्पष्ट लक्ष्य इस बात का कारण हैं कि मार्केटिंग बजट चुपचाप कैसे गायब हो जाते हैं।

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: विभाजन, लक्ष्यीकरण, स्थिति निर्धारण (STP) — यह किसके लिए है?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: बाजार को ऐसे समूहों में विभाजित करें जो अलग-अलग व्यवहार करते हैं (विभाजन), उन लोगों को चुनें जिन्हें आप वास्तव में जीत सकते हैं और लाभ के साथ सेवा कर सकते हैं (लक्ष्यीकरण), फिर उस एक विचार का निर्णय लें जिसके मालिक आप उनके दिमाग में बनना चाहते हैं (स्थिति निर्धारण)।

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: पोजीशनिंग इस बारे में एक विकल्प है कि आप क्या *नहीं* होंगे।

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: जो ब्रांड प्रीमियम, सस्ता, सबसे तेज़ और सबसे स्वस्थ है, वह इनमें से कुछ भी नहीं है।

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: मार्केटिंग मिक्स — हम वास्तव में क्या करेंगे?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: क्लासिक **4 Ps**: उत्पाद (यह क्या है, यह क्या वादा करता है), मूल्य (इसकी कीमत क्या है और यह क्या संकेत देता है), स्थान (लोग इसे कहाँ और कैसे प्राप्त कर सकते हैं, प्रचार (वे इसके बारे में कैसे सुनते हैं)।

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: सेवाएँ अक्सर तीन और P जोड़ती हैं — लोग, प्रक्रिया, भौतिक साक्ष्य — क्योंकि बाल कटवाने या दंत चिकित्सक की यात्रा में, अनुभव ही उत्पाद *है*।

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: एक अच्छी योजना की परीक्षा सुसंगतता है: चारों P को एक ही कहानी बतानी चाहिए।

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: बजट और नियंत्रण — इसकी लागत क्या होगी, और हम कैसे जानते हैं कि यह काम कर गया?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: पैसा, समयरेखा, मालिक, और वे मेट्रिक्स जिनकी आप जाँच करेंगे।

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: नियंत्रण चरण वह है जिसे लोग छोड़ देते हैं, और यह वह है जो मार्केटिंग को लागत केंद्र से एक अनुशासन में बदल देता है।

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: योजनाएँ परिकल्पनाएँ हैं।

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: नियंत्रण प्रयोग है।

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: पूरा सेमेस्टर यही है: स्थिति पर शोध करें, किसी ग्राहक को चुनें, एक सुसंगत प्रस्ताव बनाएँ, जानबूझकर खर्च करें, और ईमानदारी से मापें।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## दैनिक जीवन में

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए कि आप ऑस्टिन में एक छोटे कॉफी ब्रांड **Barton Springs Cold Brew** को चलाते हैं।

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: आप देश भर में ऑनलाइन बेचते हैं और मध्य टेक्सास की एक दर्जन किराने की दुकानों में शेल्फ पर बैठते हैं।

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: पिछली तिमाही में आपने $40,000 का राजस्व अर्जित किया था।

segments.src: You want $60,000.
Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: एक पन्ने पर योजना यहाँ है।

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **स्थिति:** कोल्ड ब्रू की भीड़ है, और बड़े राष्ट्रीय ब्रांड किराने के गलियारे के मालिक हैं।

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: लेकिन आपके बार-बार आने वाले ग्राहक एक बात की प्रशंसा करते हैं - यह कम एसिड वाला है, और संवेदनशील पेट वाले लोग इसे काला पी सकते हैं।

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: प्रतियोगी "बोल्ड" और "अतिरिक्त कैफीन" चिल्ला रहे हैं।

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: कोई भी "कोमल" नहीं चिल्ला रहा है।

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **उद्देश्य:** 31 दिसंबर तक तिमाही राजस्व को $40K से बढ़ाकर $60K करना, जिसमें कम से कम 40% बार-बार आने वाले ग्राहकों से आता हो।

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** कॉलेज के छात्र ऊर्जा चाहने वालों को छोड़ें - यह एक मूल्य युद्ध है जिसे आप हार जाएंगे।

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: टेक्सास महानगरों में 30-50 वर्ष की आयु के दैनिक कॉफी पीने वालों को लक्षित करें जिन्होंने अपने पेट की ख़राबी के कारण कॉफी कम कर दी है।

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: *उस कोल्ड ब्रू के रूप में स्थिति बनाएं जिसे आप बिना पछतावे के हर सुबह पी सकते हैं।*

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **मार्केटिंग मिक्स:** उत्पाद — पीछे दबे होने के बजाय सामने के लेबल पर "कम-एसिड, आपके पेट पर चिकना" रखें।

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: मूल्य — 4-पैक सदस्यता के लिए $32 पर होल्ड करें; छूट प्रीमियम दावे को कम कर देगी।

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: स्थान — राष्ट्रीय वितरण के पीछे भागने के बजाय स्वास्थ्य के प्रति जागरूक ज़िप कोड में H-E-B स्टोर पर दोगुना ध्यान दें, जिसे आप सेवा नहीं दे सकते।

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: प्रचार — इंस्टाग्राम पर ग्राहक प्रशंसापत्र और दो ऑस्टिन रनिंग क्लबों के साथ साझेदारी।

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **बजट और नियंत्रण:** तिमाही के लिए $9,000।

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: और यहाँ वह संख्या है जो सब कुछ तय करती है:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: नए ग्राहक को आपकी पहली बिक्री **लगभग 40 सेंट खो देती है।** यह स्वचालित रूप से विफलता नहीं है — यह केवल तभी विफलता है जब वे कभी वापस नहीं आते हैं।

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: प्रति वर्ष औसतन 2.5 ऑर्डर पर, आजीवन योगदान लगभग `2.5 x $17.60 = $44` है, जो अधिग्रहण करने के लिए $18 के मुकाबले है - लगभग 2.4 से 1।

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: योजना *तभी* काम करती है जब प्रतिधारण बना रहता है।

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: इसलिए जिस मीट्रिक को आप साप्ताहिक रूप से देखते हैं वह इंप्रेशन या पसंद नहीं है।

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: यह दूसरी-क्रम दर है।

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: मार्केटिंग प्लान वास्तव में यही करता है: यह उस धारणा को बाहर खींचता है जिस पर आप चुपचाप भरोसा कर रहे थे, जहाँ आप इसका परीक्षण कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति री कैप

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. एक मार्केटिंग प्लान एक श्रृंखला है — स्थिति, उद्देश्य, STP, मार्केटिंग मिक्स, बजट और नियंत्रण — और कहीं भी एक कम कड़ी पूरी चीज़ को तोड़ देती है।

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. पोजीशनिंग का मतलब यह तय करना है कि आप क्या नहीं होंगे; 4 P को उस एक विकल्प को मजबूत करना चाहिए।

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. उस नंबर को लिखें जिस पर आपकी योजना निर्भर करती है, फिर उसे मापें — एक अनटेस्टेड योजना सिर्फ बजट के साथ एक राय है।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ सेल्फ-क्विज़

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a properly written marketing objective?
segments.tr: **Q1.** इनमें से कौन सा ठीक से लिखा गया मार्केटिंग उद्देश्य है?

segments.src: ① Become the most loved coffee brand in Texas
segments.tr: ① टेक्सास में सबसे पसंदीदा कॉफी ब्रांड बनें

segments.src: ② Increase brand awareness significantly
segments.tr: ② ब्रांड जागरूकता में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि करें

segments.src: ③ Raise repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by December 31
segments.tr: ③ 31 दिसंबर तक बार-बार खरीदारी की दर 22% से बढ़ाकर 30% करें

segments.src: ④ Beat our competitors
segments.tr: ④ अपने प्रतिस्पर्धियों को हराएं

segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) यदि किसी कंपनी की ग्राहक अधिग्रहण लागत एक ऑर्डर पर योगदान मार्जिन से अधिक है, तो मार्केटिंग योजना निश्चित रूप से पैसा खो रही है।

segments.src: **Q3.** A brand positions itself as "affordable everyday value," then launches in luxury department stores at a premium price.
segments.tr: **Q3.** एक ब्रांड खुद को "किफायती रोजमर्रा के मूल्य" के रूप में स्थापित करता है, फिर प्रीमियम कीमत पर लग्जरी डिपार्टमेंट स्टोर में लॉन्च होता है।

segments.src: Which principle does this violate?
segments.tr: यह किस सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन करता है?

segments.src: ① Segmentation must come before targeting
segments.tr: ① विभाजन को लक्ष्यीकरण से पहले आना चाहिए

segments.src: ② The elements of the marketing mix must be consistent with the positioning
segments.tr: ② मार्केटिंग मिक्स के तत्व पोजीशनिंग के अनुरूप होने चाहिए

segments.src: ③ Objectives must be measurable
segments.tr: ③ उद्देश्य मापने योग्य होने चाहिए

segments.src: ④ The situation analysis must include competitors
segments.tr: ④ स्थिति विश्लेषण में प्रतियोगियों को शामिल करना चाहिए

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज के शब्द

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **मार्केटिंग प्लान** — एक लिखित दस्तावेज जिसमें स्थिति, उद्देश्य, लक्ष्य ग्राहक, मार्केटिंग क्रियाएं, बजट और परिणामों का न्याय करने के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले मैट्रिक्स को रेखांकित किया गया है।

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5 Cs** — एक स्थिति-विश्लेषण चेकलिस्ट: कंपनी, ग्राहक, प्रतियोगी, सहयोगी, संदर्भ।

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — विभाजन, लक्ष्यीकरण, स्थिति निर्धारण: बाजार को विभाजित करना, सेवा देने के लिए चुनना, और उस विचार को परिभाषित करना जिसके मालिक आप उनके दिमाग में बनना चाहते हैं।

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **मार्केटिंग मिक्स (4 Ps)** — उत्पाद, मूल्य, स्थान, प्रचार; नियंत्रणीय लीवर जो एक कंपनी अपनी स्थिति को पूरा करने के लिए उपयोग करती है।

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC और LTV** — ग्राहक अधिग्रहण लागत बनाम जीवन भर का योगदान जो एक ग्राहक उत्पन्न करता है; उनके बीच का अनुपात आपको बताता है कि विकास टिकाऊ है या सिर्फ महंगा।

segments.tr: *उत्तर: Q1 — ③.

segments.src: It names a metric, a starting point, a target, and a deadline; the others are aspirations without a way to check them.
segments.tr: यह एक मीट्रिक, एक शुरुआती बिंदु, एक लक्ष्य और एक समय सीमा का नाम देता है; अन्य लोगों के पास उनकी जांच करने का कोई तरीका नहीं है।

es.title: [Marketing 101 #15] La clase final: resume todo un semestre en una sola página

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > Un plan de marketing consta de cinco respuestas sinceras —dónde estamos, para quién somos, qué ofreceremos, cuánto cuesta y cómo sabremos que funcionó— escritas donde todos puedan verlas.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El concepto de hoy

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: Todas las ideas de marketing que hayas escuchado intentan responder a una sola pregunta: **¿por qué un extraño te daría su dinero en lugar de dárselo a otra persona?**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: Un plan de marketing es el documento que te obliga a responderla en voz alta.

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: La mayoría sigue el mismo esqueleto, y cada hueso corresponde a algo que los especialistas en marketing estudian durante todo el semestre:

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: Análisis de la situación: ¿dónde estamos realmente?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: La abreviatura común son las **5 C**: Compañía (en qué somos buenos realmente), Clientes (quién compra y por qué), Competidores (quién más resuelve esto), Colaboradores (distribuidores, minoristas, agencias) y Contexto (economía, regulación, tecnología, cultura).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: Muchos equipos comprimen esto en un FODA —fortalezas, oportunidades, debilidades, amenazas—, pero el FODA es un resumen de investigación, no un sustituto de ella.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: Si tu análisis de situación no tiene números, es un tablero de inspiración.

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: Objetivos: ¿cómo es ganar?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: "Aumentar el conocimiento" no es un objetivo; es un deseo.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: Un objetivo tiene un número, una métrica y una fecha límite: *aumentar la tasa de compras repetidas del 22% al 30% para el cuarto trimestre.* Las metas vagas son la razón por la cual los presupuestos de marketing desaparecen silenciosamente.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: Segmentación, Mercado Meta y Posicionamiento (STP): ¿para quién es esto?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: Divide el mercado en grupos que se comporten de manera diferente (segmentación), elige aquellos a los que realmente puedas ganar y servir de manera rentable (mercado meta), y luego decide la única idea que quieres poseer en sus mentes (posicionamiento).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: El posicionamiento es una elección sobre lo que *no* serás.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: Una marca que es prémium, barata, la más rápida y la más saludable no es ninguna de esas cosas.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: La mezcla de marketing: ¿qué haremos realmente?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: Las clásicas **4 P**: Producto (qué es, qué promete), Precio (lo que cuesta y lo que eso señala), Plaza (dónde y cómo la gente puede obtenerlo), Promoción (cómo se enteran de él).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: Los servicios a menudo añaden tres P más —Personas, Proceso, Evidencia física— porque en un corte de pelo o una visita al dentista, la experiencia *es* el producto.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: La prueba de un buen plan es la coherencia: las cuatro P deben contar la misma historia.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: Presupuesto y control: ¿cuánto costará y cómo sabemos que funcionó?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: Dinero, cronograma, responsables y las métricas que verificarás.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: El paso de control es el que la gente se salta, y es el que convierte al marketing de un centro de costos en una disciplina.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: Los planes son hipótesis.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: El control es el experimento.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: Eso es todo el semestre: investigar la situación, elegir un cliente, construir una oferta coherente, gastar deliberadamente y medir con honestidad.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: Supongamos que diriges **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, una pequeña marca de café en Austin.

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: Vendes en línea a nivel nacional y estás en los estantes de una docena de tiendas de comestibles en el centro de Texas.

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: El trimestre pasado tuviste $40,000 en ingresos.

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: Quieres $60,000.

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: Aquí está el plan en una sola página.

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **Situación:** El café en frío está saturado y las grandes marcas nacionales dominan el pasillo del supermercado.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: Pero tus clientes recurrentes elogian una cosa: es bajo en acidez y las personas con estómagos sensibles pueden beberlo negro.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: Los competidores gritan "audaz" y "cafesína extra".

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: Nadie grita "suave".

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **Objetivo:** Aumentar los ingresos trimestrales de $40K a $60K para el 31 de diciembre, con al menos un 40% procedente de clientes recurrentes.

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** Omite a los buscadores de energía universitarios; esa es una guerra de precios que perderás.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: Dirígete a bebedores diarios de café de 35 a 55 años en las metrópolis de Texas que han reducido el consumo de café porque les irrita el estómago.

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: Posiciónate como *el café en frío que puedes beber todas las mañanas sin arrepentirte*.

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **Mezcla de marketing:** Producto: coloca "bajo en acidez, suave para el estómago" en la etiqueta frontal, no enterrado en la parte posterior.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: Precio: mantén en $32 una suscripción de 4 paquetes; un descuento socavaría la afirmación prémium.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: Plaza: redobla la apuesta en las tiendas H-E-B en códigos postales conscientes de la salud en lugar de perseguir una distribución nacional que no puedes atender.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: Promoción: testimonios de clientes en Instagram y una asociación con dos clubes de corredores de Austin.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **Presupuesto y control:** $9,000 para el trimestre.

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: Y este es el número que lo decide todo:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: Tu primera venta a un cliente nuevo **pierde unos 40 centavos.** Eso no es automáticamente un fracaso; solo es un fracaso si nunca regresan.

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: Con un promedio de 2.5 pedidos por año, la contribución de por vida es de aproximadamente `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, frente a $18 para adquirirlo, es decir, alrededor de 2.4 a 1.

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: El plan funciona *solo* si la retención se mantiene.

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: Por lo tanto, la métrica que observas semanalmente no son las impresiones o los “me gusta”.

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: Es la tasa de pedidos secundarios.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: Eso es lo que realmente hace un plan de marketing: saca a la luz la suposición en la que confiabas en silencio, donde puedes probarla.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. Un plan de marketing es una cadena —situación, objetivos, STP, mezcla de marketing, presupuesto y control— y un eslabón débil en cualquier parte rompe todo.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. El posicionamiento significa decidir lo que no serás; las 4 P deben reforzar esa única elección.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. Escribe el número del que depende tu plan, luego médelo; un plan no probado es solo una opinión con presupuesto.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a properly written marketing objective?
segments.tr: **P1.** ¿Cuál de estos es un objetivo de marketing redactado adecuadamente?

segments.src: ① Become the most loved coffee brand in Texas
segments.tr: ① Convertirse en la marca de café más querida en Texas

segments.src: ② Increase brand awareness significantly
segments.tr: ② Aumentar significativamente el conocimiento de marca

segments.src: ③ Raise repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by December 31
segments.tr: ③ Elevar la tasa de compras repetidas del 22% al 30% para el 31 de diciembre

segments.src: ④ Beat our competitors
segments.tr: ④ Superar a nuestros competidores

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) If a company's customer acquisition cost is higher than the contribution margin on a single order, the marketing plan is definitely losing money.
segments.tr: **P2.** (V/F) Si el costo de adquisición de clientes de una empresa es mayor que el margen de contribución en un solo pedido, el plan de marketing definitivamente está perdiendo dinero.

segments.src: **Q3.** A brand positions itself as "affordable everyday value," then launches in luxury department stores at a premium price.
segments.tr: **P3.** Una marca se posiciona como "valor diario asequible", luego se lanza en grandes almacenes de lujo a un precio prémium.

segments.src: Which principle does this violate?
segments.tr: ¿Qué principio viola esto?

segments.src: ① Segmentation must come before targeting
segments.tr: ① La segmentación debe venir antes de la selección del mercado meta

segments.src: ② The elements of the marketing mix must be consistent with the positioning
segments.tr: ② Los elementos de la mezcla de marketing deben ser coherentes con el posicionamiento

segments.src: ③ Objectives must be measurable
segments.tr: ③ Los objetivos deben ser medibles

segments.src: ④ The situation analysis must include competitors
segments.tr: ④ El análisis de situación debe incluir a los competidores

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de hoy

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **Plan de marketing** — Un documento escrito que expone la situación, los objetivos, el cliente objetivo, las acciones de marketing, el presupuesto y las métricas utilizadas para juzgar los resultados.

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5 C** — Una lista de verificación de análisis de situación: Compañía, Clientes, Competidores, Colaboradores, Contexto.

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — Segmentación, Mercado Meta y Posicionamiento: dividir el mercado, elegir a quién servir y definir la idea que deseas poseer en sus mentes.

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **Mezcla de marketing (4 P)** — Producto, Precio, Plaza, Promoción; las palancas controlables que una empresa utiliza para cumplir con su posicionamiento.

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC y LTV** — Costo de adquisición de clientes versus la contribución de por vida que genera un cliente; la relación entre ambos te dice si el crecimiento es sostenible o simplemente costoso.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 — ③.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: P1 — ③.

segments.src: It names a metric, a starting point, a target, and a deadline; the others are aspirations without a way to check them.
segments.tr: Nombra una métrica, un punto de partida, un objetivo y una fecha límite; los demás son aspiraciones sin una forma de verificarlos.

segments.src: It's a warning sign, not a verdict.
segments.tr: Es una señal de advertencia, no un veredicto.

segments.tr: Si los clientes compran repetidamente, la contribución de por vida puede superar cómodamente el costo de adquisición, que es exactamente el caso de Barton Springs, pero el plan vive o muere según la retención.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: لنفترض أنك تدير **Barton Springs Cold Brew**، علامة تجارية صغيرة للقهوة في أوستن.

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: أنت تبيع عبر الإنترنت على مستوى البلاد وتتواجد على أرفف عشرات متاجر البقالة في وسط تكساس.

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: في الربع الأخير حققت 40,000 دولار من الإيرادات.

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: أنت تريد 60,000 دولار.

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: إليك الخطة في صفحة واحدة.

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **الموقف:** القهوة الباردة سوق مزدحم، والعلامات التجارية الوطنية الكبيرة تسيطر على ممرات البقالة.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: لكن عملائك المتكررين يشيدون بشيء واحد — أنها منخفضة الحموضة، ويمكن للأشخاص ذوي المعدة الحساسة شربها سوداء.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: المنافسون يصرخون بكلمات "جريئة" و"كافيين إضافي".

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: لا أحد يصرخ بكلمة "لطيفة".

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **الهدف:** زيادة الإيرادات الربع سنوية من 40 ألف دولار إلى 60 ألف دولار بحلول 31 ديسمبر، مع حصول ما لا يقل عن 40% منها من العملاء المتكررين.

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** تخطَّ الباحثين عن الطاقة من طلاب الجامعات — فهذه حرب أسعار ستخسرها.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: استهدف شاربي القهوة اليوميين الذين تتراوح أعمارهم بين 30 و55 عاماً في مدن تكساس الذين قللوا من شرب القهوة لأنها تزعج معدتهم.

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: تموضع كـ *القهوة الباردة التي يمكنك شربها كل صباح دون ندم*.

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **المزيج التسويقي:** المنتج — ضع "منخفضة الحموضة، لطيفة على معدتك" على الملصق الأمامي، وليس مدفوناً في الخلف.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: السعر — حافظ على 32 دولاراً لاشتراك 4 عبوات؛ الخصم سيقوض ادعاء الجودة العالية.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: المكان — ضاعف الجهود في متاجر H-E-B في الرموز البريدية المهتمة بالصحة بدلاً من مطاردة التوزيع الوطني الذي لا يمكنك خدمته.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: الترويج — شهادات العملاء على إنستغرام وشراكة مع ناديين للجري في أوستن.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **الميزانية والتحكم:** 9,000 دولار للربع.

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: وهذا هو الرقم الذي يقرر كل شيء:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: عمليتك الأولى لبيع لعميل جديد **تخسر حوالي 40 سنتاً.** هذا ليس فشلاً تلقائياً — إنه فشل فقط إذا لم يعودوا أبداً.

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: بمتوسط 2.5 طلب في السنة، المساهمة مدى الحياة هي تقريباً `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`، مقابل 18 دولاراً للاستحواذ — حوالي 2.4 إلى 1.

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: الخطة تنجح *فقط* إذا استمر الاحتفاظ بالعملاء.

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: لذا المقياس الذي تراقبه أسبوعياً ليس الانطباعات أو الإعجابات.

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: إنه معدل الطلب الثاني.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: هذا ما تفعله خطة التسويق حقاً: إنها تسحب الافتراض الذي كنت تعتمد عليه بهدوء إلى العلن، حيث يمكنك اختباره.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. خطة التسويق هي سلسلة — الموقف، الأهداف، STP، المزيج التسويقي، الميزانية والتحكم — وأي حلقة ضعيفة في أي مكان تكسر السلسلة بأكملها.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. التموضع يعني تحديد ما لن تكون عليه؛ يجب أن تعزز الـ 4 Ps هذا الخيار الواحد.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. اكتب الرقم الذي تعتمد عليه خطتك، ثم قسه — الخطة غير المختبرة هي مجرد رأي بميزانية.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: **س1.** أي من هذه أهداف تسويقية مكتوبة بشكل صحيح؟

segments.src: ① Become the most loved coffee brand in Texas
segments.tr: ① أن تصبح علامة القهوة الأكثر حباً في تكساس

segments.src: ② Increase brand awareness significantly
segments.tr: ② زيادة الوعي بالعلامة التجارية بشكل كبير

segments.src: ③ Raise repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by December 31
segments.tr: ③ رفع معدل تكرار الشراء من 22% إلى 30% بحلول 31 ديسمبر

segments.src: ④ Beat our competitors
segments.tr: ④ التغلب على منافسينا

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) If a company's customer acquisition cost is higher than the contribution margin on a single order, the marketing plan is definitely losing money.
segments.tr: **س2.** (صح/خطأ) إذا كانت تكلفة الاستحواذ على العميل أعلى من هامش المساهمة في طلب واحد، فإن خطة التسويق تخسر المال بالتأكيد.

segments.src: **Q3.** A brand positions itself as "affordable everyday value," then launches in luxury department stores at a premium price.
segments.tr: **س3.** علامة تجارية تتموضع كـ "قيمة يومية معقولة"، ثم تطلق في متاجر فاخرة بسعر مرتفع.

segments.src: Which principle does this violate?
segments.tr: أي مبدأ ينتهك هذا؟

segments.src: ① Segmentation must come before targeting
segments.tr: ① يجب أن يأتي التقسيم قبل الاستهداف

segments.src: ② The elements of the marketing mix must be consistent with the positioning
segments.tr: ② يجب أن تكون عناصر المزيج التسويقي متسقة مع التموضع

segments.src: ③ Objectives must be measurable
segments.tr: ③ يجب أن تكون الأهداف قابلة للقياس

segments.src: ④ The situation analysis must include competitors
segments.tr: ④ يجب أن يتضمن تحليل الموقف المنافسين

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **خطة التسويق** — وثيقة مكتوبة توضح الموقف، الأهداف، العميل المستهدف، الإجراءات التسويقية، الميزانية، والمقاييس المستخدمة للحكم على النتائج.

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5 Cs** — قائمة مرجعية لتحليل الموقف: الشركة، العملاء، المنافسون، المتعاونون، السياق.

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — التقسيم، الاستهداف، التموضع: تقسيم السوق، اختيار من تخدم، وتحديد الفكرة التي تريد امتلاكها في أذهانهم.

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **المزيج التسويقي (4 Ps)** — المنتج، السعر، المكان، الترويج؛ الروافع القابلة للتحكم التي تستخدمها الشركة لتحقيق تموضعها.

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC و LTV** — تكلفة الاستحواذ على العميل مقابل المساهمة مدى الحياة التي يولدها العميل؛ النسبة بينهما تخبرك ما إذا كان النمو مستداماً أم مجرد مكلف.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 — ③.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: س1 — ③.

segments.src: It names a metric, a starting point, a target, and a deadline; the others are aspirations without a way to check them.
segments.tr: إنها تسمي مقياساً، ونقطة بداية، وهدفاً، وموعداً نهائياً؛ البقية هي تطلعات دون طريقة للتحقق منها.

segments.src: Q2 — X.
segments.tr: س2 — خطأ.

segments.src: It's a warning sign, not a verdict.
segments.tr: إنها علامة تحذير، وليست حكماً نهائياً.

segments.src: If customers buy repeatedly, lifetime contribution can comfortably exceed acquisition cost, which is exactly the Barton Springs case — but the plan then lives or dies on retention.
segments.tr: إذا اشترى العملاء بشكل متكرر، يمكن للمساهمة مدى الحياة أن تتجاوز تكلفة الاستحواذ بشكل مريح، وهو بالضبط حالة Barton Springs — لكن الخطة تعيش أو تموت بناءً على الاحتفاظ بالعملاء.

segments.src: Q3 — ②.
segments.tr: س3 — ②.

segments.tr: ادعاء التموضع وقرارات السعر/المكان تتناقض مع بعضها البعض، لذا لا يحصل العملاء على قصة واضحة حول ماهية العلامة التجارية.*

fr.title: [Marketing 101 #15] La dernière leçon : Résumer un semestre entier sur une seule page

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > Un plan marketing se résume à cinq réponses honnêtes — où nous en sommes, à qui nous nous adressons, ce que nous offrons, combien cela coûte et comment nous saurons que cela a fonctionné — consignées là où tout le monde peut les voir.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept du jour

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: Toute idée marketing que vous avez entendue essaie de répondre à une seule question : **pourquoi un inconnu vous donnerait-il de l'argent plutôt qu'à quelqu'un d'autre ?**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: Un plan marketing est le document qui vous force à y répondre à voix haute.

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: La plupart suivent le même squelette, et chaque os correspond à quelque chose que les spécialistes du marketing étudient tout au semestre :

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: Analyse de la situation — où en sommes-nous vraiment ?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: Le terme abrégé courant est les **5 C** : Entreprise (ce en quoi nous sommes vraiment bons), Clients (qui achète et pourquoi), Concurrents (qui d'autre résout ce problème), Collaborateurs (distributeurs, détaillants, agences) et Contexte (économie, réglementation, technologie, culture).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: De nombreuses équipes compressent cela en une analyse SWOT — forces, faiblesses, opportunités, menaces — mais le SWOT est un résumé de recherche, pas un substitut.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: Si votre analyse de situation ne contient aucun chiffre, c'est un tableau d'inspiration.

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: Objectifs — à quoi ressemble la victoire ?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: "Développer la notoriété" n'est pas un objectif ; c'est un souhait.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: Un objectif comporte un chiffre, une métrique et une date limite : *augmenter le taux d'achat répété de 22 % à 30 % d'ici le T4.* Les objectifs vagues sont la raison pour laquelle les budgets marketing disparaissent discrètement.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: Segmentation, Ciblage, Positionnement (STP) — à qui s'adresse ce produit ?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: Divisez le marché en groupes qui se comportent différemment (segmentation), choisissez ceux que vous pouvez réellement gagner et servir de manière rentable (ciblage), puis décidez de l'idée unique que vous voulez incarner dans leur esprit (positionnement).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: Le positionnement est un choix sur ce que vous ne *serez pas*.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: Une marque qui est haut de gamme, bon marché, la plus rapide et la plus saine n'est rien de tout cela.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: Le mix marketing — que allons-nous réellement faire ?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: Les **4 P** classiques : Produit (ce que c'est, ce qu'il promet), Prix (combien il coûte et ce que cela signiguiie), Place / Distribution (où et comment les gens peuvent l'obtenir), Promotion (comment ils en entendent parler).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: Les services ajoutent souvent trois P supplémentaires — Personnes, Processus, Preuve physique — car dans une coupe de cheveux ou une visite chez le dentiste, l'expérience *est* le produit.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: Le test d'un bon plan est la cohérence : les quatre P doivent tous raconter la même histoire.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: Budget et contrôle — combien cela va-t-il coûter et comment savons-nous que cela a fonctionné ?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: Argent, calendrier, responsables et mesures que vous vérifierez.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: L'étape du contrôle est celle que les gens omettent, et c'est celle qui transforme le marketing d'un centre de coûts en une discipline.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: Les plans sont des hypothèses.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: Le contrôle est l'expérience.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: C'est tout le semestre : étudier la situation, choisir un client, construire une offre cohérente, dépenser délibérément et mesurer honnêtement.
