pt.title: [Marketing 101 #15] A Aula Final: Coloque um Semestre Inteiro em Uma Página

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > Um plano de marketing são apenas cinco respostas honestas — onde estamos, para quem somos, o que vamos oferecer, quanto custa e como saberemos que funcionou — anotadas onde todos possam ver.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: Todas as ideias de marketing que você já ouviu tentam responder a uma pergunta: **por que um estranho daria dinheiro a você em vez de dar a outra pessoa?**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: Um plano de marketing é o documento que força você a responder a isso em voz alta.

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: A maioria deles segue o mesmo esqueleto, e cada osso corresponde a algo que os profissionais de marketing estudam o semestre todo:

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: Análise da situação — onde estamos, de verdade?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: A abreviação comum são os **5 Cs**: Empresa (no que somos realmente bons), Clientes (quem compra e por quê), Concorrentes (quem mais resolve isso), Colaboradores (distribuidores, varejistas, agências) e Contexto (economia, regulamentação, tecnologia, cultura).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: Muitas equipes comprimem isso em uma SWOT — forças, fraquezas, oportunidades, ameaças —, mas a SWOT é um resumo de pesquisa, não um substituto para ela.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: Se a sua análise de situação não tiver números, ela é um mural de inspiração (mood board).

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: Objetivos — com o que se parece a vitória?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: "Aumentar a conscientização" não é um objetivo; é um desejo.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: Um objetivo tem um número, uma métrica e um prazo: *aumentar a taxa de recompra de 22% para 30% até o 4º trimestre.* Metas vagas são a forma como os budgets de marketing desaparecem silenciosamente.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: Segmentação, Posicionamento e Alvejamento (STP) — para quem é isso?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: Divida o mercado em grupos que se comportam de maneira diferente (segmentação), escolha aqueles que você realmente pode vencer e atender de forma lucrativa (alvejamento/target), e então decida a única ideia que você quer possuir na mente deles (posicionamento).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: Posicionamento é uma escolha sobre o que você *não* será.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: Uma marca que é premium, barata, a mais rápida e a mais saudável não é nenhuma dessas coisas.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: O mix de marketing — o que realmente faremos?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: Os clássicos **4 Ps**: Produto (o que é, o que promete), Preço (quanto custa e o que isso sinaliza), Praça (onde e como as pessoas podem conseguir), Promoção (como ficam sabendo).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: Serviços frequentemente adicionam mais três Ps — Pessoas, Processo, Evidência física — porque em um corte de cabelo ou consulta ao dentista, a experiência *é* o produto.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: O teste de um bom plano é a coerência: os quatro Ps devem estar todos contando a mesma história.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: Orçamento e controle — quanto custará e como sabemos que funcionou?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: Dinheiro, cronograma, responsáveis e as métricas que você vai verificar.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: A etapa de controle é a que as pessoas pulam, e é ela que transforma o marketing de um centro de custos em uma disciplina.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: Planos são hipóteses.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: O controle é o experimento.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: Esse é o semestre inteiro: pesquise a situação, escolha um cliente, construa uma oferta coerente, gaste deliberadamente e meça com honestidade.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Quotidiana

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: Digamos que você gerencie o **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, uma pequena marca de café em Austin.

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: Você vende online em todo o país e está nas prateleiras de uma dúzia de supermercados no centro do Texas.

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: No último trimestre, você faturou $40.000 em receita.

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: Você quer $60.000.

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: Aqui está o plano em uma página.

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **Situação:** O mercado de cold brew está lotado, e grandes marcas nacionais dominam os corredores dos supermercados.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: Mas seus clientes recorrentes elogiam uma coisa — é de baixa acidez, e pessoas com estômagos sensíveis podem tomá-lo puro.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: Concorrentes estão gritando "forte" e "cafeína extra".

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: Ninguém está gritando "suave".

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **Objetivo:** Aumentar a receita trimestral de $40K para $60K até 31 de dezembro, com pelo menos 40% vindo de clientes recorrentes.

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** Pule os buscadores de energia universitários — essa é uma guerra de preços que você vai perder.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: Alveje bebedores diários de café de 30 a 55 anos nas metrópoles do Texas que reduziram o consumo de café porque ele irrita o estômago.

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: Posicione-se como *o cold brew que você pode tomar todas as manhãs sem se arrepender*.

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **Mix de marketing:** Produto — coloque "baixa acidez, suave para o seu estômago" no rótulo frontal, não escondido atrás.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: Preço — mantenha em $32 para uma assinatura de 4 pacotes; um desconto prejudicaria a alegação premium.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: Praça — aposte forte nas lojas H-E-B em CEPs preocupados com a saúde, em vez de correr atrás de distribuição nacional que você não consegue atender.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: Promoção — depoimentos de clientes no Instagram e uma parceria com dois clubes de corrida de Austin.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **Orçamento e controle:** $9.000 para o trimestre.

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: E aqui está o número que decide tudo:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: Sua primeira venda para um novo cliente **perde cerca de 40 centavos.** Isso não é automaticamente um fracasso — só é um fracasso se eles nunca voltarem.

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: A uma média de 2,5 pedidos por ano, a contribuição vitalícia é de aproximadamente `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, contra $18 para adquirir — cerca de 2,4 para 1.

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: O plano funciona *apenas* se a retenção se mantiver.

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: Portanto, a métrica que você observa semanalmente não são impressões ou curtidas.

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: É a taxa de segunda ordem.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: É isso que um plano de marketing realmente faz: ele arrasta a premissa em que você confiava silenciosamente para o aberto, onde você pode testá-la.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Recapitulação de Três Linhas

segments.tr: 1. Um plano de marketing é uma corrente — situação, objetivos, STP, mix de marketing, orçamento e controle — e um elo fraco em qualquer lugar quebra tudo.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. Posicionamento significa decidir o que você não será; os 4 Ps devem reforçar essa única escolha.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. Anote o número de que seu plano depende e, em seguida, meça-o — um plano não testado é apenas uma opinião com um orçamento.

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: Analisis situasi — di mana sebenarnya posisi kita?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: Singkatan umumnya adalah **5 C**: Perusahaan (apa keahlian nyata kita), Pelanggan (siapa yang membeli dan mengapa), Pesaing (siapa lagi yang menyelesaikan masalah ini), Kolaborator (distributor, peritel, agen), dan Konteks (ekonomi, regulasi, teknologi, budaya).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: Banyak tim yang meringkas ini menjadi SWOT — kekuatan, kelemahan, peluang, ancaman — tetapi SWOT adalah ringkasan dari riset, bukan penggantinya.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: Jika analisis situasi Anda tidak memiliki angka di dalamnya, itu hanyalah papan suasana (mood board).

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: Tujuan — seperti apakah bentuk kemenangan itu?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: "Meningkatkan kesadaran" bukanlah sebuah tujuan; itu adalah sebuah harapan.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: Sebuah tujuan memiliki angka, metrik, dan tenggat waktu: *meningkatkan tingkat pembelian berulang dari 22% menjadi 30% pada Q4.* Tujuan yang samar adalah cara anggaran pemasaran lenyap secara diam-diam.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: Segmentasi, Penargetan, Posisioning (STP) — untuk siapa ini ditujukan?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: Bagi pasar menjadi kelompok-kelompok yang berperilaku berbeda (segmentasi), pilih kelompok yang benar-benar dapat Anda menangkan dan layani dengan menguntungkan (penargetan), lalu tentukan satu ide yang ingin Anda kuasai di benak mereka (posisioning).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: Posisioning adalah pilihan tentang hal apa yang *tidak* akan Anda miliki.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: Merek yang premium, murah, tercepat, dan paling sehat bukanlah dari semua hal tersebut.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: Bauran pemasaran — apa yang sebenarnya akan kita lakukan?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: Klasik **4 P**: Produk (apa bentuknya, apa janjinya), Harga (berapa biayanya dan apa sinyal yang diberikan), Tempat (di mana dan bagaimana orang mendapatkannya), Promosi (bagaimana mereka mengetahuinya).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: Layanan sering kali menambahkan tiga P lagi — Orang (People), Proses (Process), Bukti fisik (Physical evidence) — karena dalam potongan rambut atau kunjungan dokter gigi, pengalaman *itulah* produknya.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: Ujian dari rencana yang baik adalah koherensi: keempat P tersebut harus menceritakan kisah yang sama.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: Anggaran dan pengendalian — berapa biayanya, dan bagaimana kita tahu hal itu berhasil?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: Uang, jadwal, penanggung jawab, dan metrik yang akan Anda periksa.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: Langkah pengendalian adalah langkah yang sering dilewati orang, padahal langkah itulah yang mengubah pemasaran dari pusat biaya menjadi sebuah disiplin ilmu.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: Rencana adalah hipotesis.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: Pengendalian adalah eksperimennya.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: Itulah keseluruhan materi satu semester: teliti situasinya, pilih pelanggan, bangun penawaran yang koheren, belanjakan dengan sengaja, dan ukur dengan jujur.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: Katakanlah Anda menjalankan **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, sebuah merek kopi kecil di Austin.

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: Anda menjual secara online secara nasional dan tersedia di rak-rak di belasan toko kelontong Texas Tengah.

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: Kuartal lalu Anda memperoleh pendapatan $40.000.

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: Anda menginginkan $60.000.

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: Berikut adalah rencananya dalam satu halaman.

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **Situasi:** Kopi seduh dingin (cold brew) sudah sangat padat, dan merek nasional besar menguasai lorong toko kelontong.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: Namun pelanggan tetap Anda memuji satu hal — kopi ini rendah asam, dan orang dengan lambung sensitif dapat meminumnya tanpa dicampur.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: Pesaing meneriakkan "kuat" dan "kafein ekstra."

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: Tidak ada yang meneriakkan "lembut."

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **Tujuan:** Meningkatkan pendapatan kuartalan dari $40K menjadi $60K paling lambat 31 Desember, dengan setidaknya 40% berasal dari pelanggan tetap.

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** Lewati pencari energi mahasiswa — itu adalah perang harga yang akan Anda kalahkan.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: Targetkan peminum kopi harian berusia 30–55 tahun di wilayah perkotaan Texas yang telah mengurangi konsumsi kopi karena membuat perut mereka sakit.

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: Posisikan sebagai *kopi seduh dingin yang dapat Anda minum setiap pagi tanpa penyesalan.*

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **Bauran pemasaran:** Produk — cantumkan "rendah asam, lembut di lambung" pada label depan, bukan disembunyikan di bagian belakang.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: Harga — pertahankan pada $32 untuk langganan 4 paket; diskon akan merusak klaim premium.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: Tempat — fokuskan pada toko H-E-B di kode pos yang peduli kesehatan daripada mengejar distribusi nasional yang tidak sanggup Anda layani.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: Promosi — testimoni pelanggan di Instagram dan kemitraan dengan dua klub lari Austin.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **Anggaran dan pengendalian:** $9.000 untuk kuartal tersebut.

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: Dan inilah angka yang menentukan segalanya:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: Penjualan pertama Anda ke pelanggan baru **rugi sekitar 40 sen.** Itu bukanlah kegagalan secara otomatis — itu hanya menjadi kegagalan jika mereka tidak pernah kembali.

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: Dengan rata-rata 2,5 pesanan per tahun, kontribusi seumur hidup adalah sekitar `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, dengan biaya akuisisi $18 — sekitar 2,4 banding 1.

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: Rencana ini *hanya* akan berhasil jika retensi bertahan.

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: Jadi metrik yang Anda amati setiap minggu bukanlah impresi atau suka (likes).

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: Melainkan tingkat pesanan kedua.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: Itulah yang sebenarnya dilakukan oleh rencana pemasaran: rencana ini menyeret asumsi yang selama ini Andaandalkan secara diam-diam ke tempat terbuka, di mana Anda dapat mengujinya.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: **Rekap Tiga Baris**

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. Rencana pemasaran adalah sebuah rantai — situasi, tujuan, STP, bauran pemasaran, anggaran dan pengendalian — dan rantai yang lemah di mana pun akan merusak semuanya.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. Posisioning berarti memutuskan hal apa yang tidak akan Anda miliki; keempat P harus memperkuat satu pilihan tersebut.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. Tuliskan angka yang menjadi sandaran rencana Anda, lalu ukurlah — rencana yang tidak diuji hanyalah sebuah opini dengan anggaran.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a properly written marketing objective?
segments.tr: **Q1.** Manakah dari berikut ini yang merupakan tujuan pemasaran yang ditulis dengan benar?

segments.src: ① Become the most loved coffee brand in Texas
segments.tr: ① Menjadi merek kopi yang paling dicintai di Texas

segments.src: ② Increase brand awareness significantly
segments.tr: ② Meningkatkan kesadaran merek secara signifikan

segments.src: ③ Raise repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by December 31
segments.tr: ③ Meningkatkan tingkat pembelian berulang dari 22% menjadi 30% paling lambat 31 Desember

segments.src: ④ Beat our competitors
segments.tr: ④ Mengalahkan pesaing kita

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) If a company's customer acquisition cost is higher than the contribution margin on a single order, the marketing plan is definitely losing money.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (B/S) Jika biaya akuisisi pelanggan suatu perusahaan lebih tinggi daripada marjin kontribusi pada satu pesanan, rencana pemasaran tersebut pasti merugi.

segments.src: **Q3.** A brand positions itself as "affordable everyday value," then launches in luxury department stores at a premium price.
segments.tr: **Q3.** Sebuah merek memposisikan dirinya sebagai "nilai sehari-hari yang terjangkau", lalu diluncurkan di department store mewah dengan harga premium.

segments.src: Which principle does this violate?
segments.tr: Prinsip mana yang dilanggar oleh hal ini?

segments.src: ① Segmentation must come before targeting
segments.tr: ① Segmentasi harus dilakukan sebelum penargetan

segments.src: ② The elements of the marketing mix must be consistent with the positioning
segments.tr: ② Elemen bauran pemasaran harus konsisten dengan posisioning

segments.src: ③ Objectives must be measurable
segments.tr: ③ Tujuan harus dapat diukur

segments.src: ④ The situation analysis must include competitors
segments.tr: ④ Analisis situasi harus mencakup pesaing

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **Rencana pemasaran** — Dokumen tertulis yang memaparkan situasi, tujuan, target pelanggan, tindakan pemasaran, anggaran, dan metrik yang digunakan untuk menilai hasil.

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5 C** — Daftar periksa analisis situasi: Perusahaan (Company), Pelanggan (Customers), Pesaing (Competitors), Kolaborator (Collaborators), Konteks (Context).

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — Segmentasi, Penargetan, Posisioning: membagi pasar, memilih siapa yang akan dilayani, dan mendefinisikan ide yang ingin Anda kuasai di benak mereka.

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **Bauran pemasaran (4 P)** — Produk (Product), Harga (Price), Tempat (Place), Promosi (Promotion); tuas yang dapat dikendalikan yang digunakan perusahaan untuk mewujudkan posisioningnya.

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC dan LTV** — Biaya akuisisi pelanggan versus kontribusi seumur hidup yang dihasilkan oleh seorang pelanggan; rasio di antara keduanya memberi tahu Anda apakah pertumbuhan tersebut berkelanjutan atau sekadar mahal.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 — ③.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: Q1 — ③.

segments.src: It names a metric, a starting point, a target, and a deadline; the others are aspirations without a way to check them.
segments.tr: Ini menyebutkan metrik, titik awal, target, dan tenggat waktu; pilihan lainnya adalah aspirasi tanpa cara untuk memeriksanya.

segments.src: Q2 — X.
segments.tr: Q2 — S.

segments.src: It's a warning sign, not a verdict.
segments.tr: Itu adalah tanda peringatan, bukan vonis akhir.

segments.src: If customers buy repeatedly, lifetime contribution can comfortably exceed acquisition cost, which is exactly the Barton Springs case — but the plan then lives or dies on retention.
segments.tr: Jika pelanggan membeli secara berulang, kontribusi seumur hidup dapat dengan mudah melebihi biaya akuisisi, yang persis seperti kasus Barton Springs — tetapi rencana tersebut kemudian hidup atau mati berdasarkan retensi.

segments.src: Q3 — ②.
segments.tr: Q3 — ②.

segments.src: The positioning claim and the price/place decisions contradict each other, so customers get no clear story about what the brand is.*
segments.tr: Klaim posisioning dan keputusan harga/tempat saling bertentangan, sehingga pelanggan tidak mendapatkan kisah yang jelas tentang apa merek tersebut.*

ja.title: [Marketing 101 #15] 最終講義：1学期全体のまとめを1ページに凝縮する

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > マーケティングプランとは、自分たちがどこにいて、誰をターゲットにし、何を提供し、いくらかかり、どうやってそれがうまくいったとわかるのかという、5つの率直な答えを、誰もが見える場所に書き出したものです。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: これまでに耳にしたことのあるあらゆるマーケティングのアイデアは、たった1つの質問に答えようとしています。**「見ず知らずの人が、なぜ他の誰かではなく、あなたにお金を払うのか？」**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: マーケティングプランとは、その質問に声に出して答えることを強制するドキュメントです。

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: そのほとんどが同じ骨組みに従っており、それぞれの骨はマーケターが1学期かけて学ぶ内容に対応しています。

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: 状況分析 — 私たちは今、本当はどこにいるのか？**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: 一般的な略語が **5 Cs** です。Company（企業：実際に何が得意か）、Customers（顧客：誰がなぜ買うのか）、Competitors（競合：ほかに誰がこれを解決しているか）、Collaborators（協力者：販売業者、小売業者、代理店）、Context（文脈：経済、規制、テクノロジー、文化）。

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: 多くのチームはこれをSWOT（強み、弱み、機会、脅威）に圧縮しますが、SWOTはリサーチの要約であり、その代わりにはなりません。

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: 状況分析に数字が含まれていない場合、それはただのムードボードに過ぎません。

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: 目標 — 勝利とはどのような状態か？**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: 「認知度を高める」は目標ではなく、単なる願いです。

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: 目標には数字、指標、締め切りが必要です。*たとえば、「Q4（第4四半期）までにリピート購入率を22%から30%に引き上げる」*。あいまいな目標こそが、マーケティング予算を静かに消滅させる原因です。

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: セグメンテーション、ターゲティング、ポジショニング（STP） — これは誰のためのものか？**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: 市場を異なる行動をとるグループに分割し（セグメンテーション）、実際に勝利して利益を上げてサービスを提供できるグループを選び（ターゲティング）、その人たちの頭の中で自分たちが占有したい1つのアイデアを決定します（ポジショニング）。

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: ポジショニングとは、自分が「何にならないか」についての選択です。

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: プレミアムであり、安価であり、最速であり、最もヘルシーであるというブランドは、そのどれでもありません。

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: マーケティングミックス — 私たちは実際に何をするのか？**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: 古典的な **4 Ps**：Product（製品：それが何であり、何を約束するか）、Price（価格：いくらかかり、それが何を示唆するか）、Place（流通：どこでどのように手に入るか）、Promotion（プロモーション：どうやってそれを知るか）。

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: サービス業では、さらに3つのP（People：人、Process：プロセス、Physical evidence：物理的証拠）が追加されることがよくあります。なぜなら、ヘアカットや歯科医院の訪問において、その体験こそが製品だからです。

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: 優れたプランのテストは一貫性です。4つのPはすべて同じストーリーを語っているべきです。

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: 予算と統制 — いくらかかり、それがうまくいったとどうやってわかるのか？**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: お金、タイムライン、担当者、そして確認する指標。

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: 統制のステップは人々が飛ばしがちなものですが、これこそがマーケティングをコストセンターから規律へと変えるものです。

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: 計画とは仮説です。

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: 統制とは実験です。

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: それが1学期全体のまとめです。状況を調査し、顧客を選び、一貫したオファーを構築し、意図的に支出を行い、正直に測定する。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活において

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: オースティンにある小さなコーヒーブランド、**Barton Springs Cold Brew**を運営していると仮定します。

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: オンラインで全国に向けて販売しており、テキサス中央部の十数件の食料品店の棚に並んでいます。

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: 前四半期の売上高は40,000ドルでした。

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: 60,000ドルにしたいと考えています。

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: これが1ページにまとめたプランです。

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: テキサスの都市部に住む30〜55歳の毎日のコーヒー飲用者で、胃の不調のためにコーヒーを控えてきた層をターゲットにします。

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **予算と統制：** 四半期で9,000ドル。

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: そして、すべてを決定づける数字がこちらです：

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: 新規顧客への最初の販売で**約40セントの赤字**になります。これは自動的に失敗というわけではありません。二度と戻ってこない場合にのみ失敗となります。

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: 年間平均2.5回の注文で、生涯貢献利益はおよそ `2.5 x $17.60 = $44` であり、獲得コストの18ドルに対して約2.4対1となります。

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: このプランが機能するのは、リテンション（継続率）が維持される場合**のみ**です。

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: したがって、毎週確認する指標は、インプレッションや「いいね！」ではありません。

segments.src: It's second-order rate.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.

de.title: [Marketing 101 #15] Die letzte Klasse: Ein ganzes Semester auf eine Seite passen

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > Ein Marketingplan besteht aus nur fünf ehrlichen Antworten – wo wir stehen, für wen wir da sind, was wir anbieten, was es kostet und woran wir erkennen, dass es funktioniert –, aufgeschrieben, wo jeder sie sehen kann.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: Jede Marketingidee, die Sie jemals gehört haben, versucht eine Frage zu beantworten: **Warum sollte ein Fremder Ihnen Geld geben, anstatt es jemand anderem zu geben?**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: Ein Marketingplan ist das Dokument, das Sie zwingt, sie laut zu beantworten.

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: Die meisten von ihnen folgen demselben Skelett, und jeder Knochen entspricht etwas, das Vermarkter ein ganzes Semester lang studieren:

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: Situationsanalyse – wo stehen wir eigentlich?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: Die gängige Abkürzung sind die **5 Cs**: Unternehmen (worin wir tatsächlich gut sind), Kunden (wer kauft und warum), Mitbewerber (wer das sonst noch löst), Partner (Vertreiber, Einzelhändler, Agenturen) und Kontext (Wirtschaft, Regulierung, Technologie, Kultur).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: Viele Teams komprimieren dies zu einer SWOT-Analyse – Stärken, Schwächen, Chancen, Bedrohungen –, aber SWOT ist eine Zusammenfassung von Forschung, kein Ersatz dafür.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: Wenn Ihre Situationsanalyse keine Zahlen enthält, ist sie ein Moodboard.

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: Ziele – wie sieht Gewinnen aus?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: „Bekanntheit steigern“ ist kein Ziel; es ist ein Wunsch.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: Ein Ziel hat eine Zahl, eine Kennzahl und eine Frist: *Erhöhung der Wiederkaufrate von 22 % auf 30 % bis zum 4. Quartal.* Vage Ziele sind der Grund, warum Marketingbudgets leise verschwinden.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: Segmentierung, Targeting, Positionierung (STP) – für wen ist das?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: Unterteilen Sie den Markt in Gruppen, die sich unterschiedlich verhalten (Segmentierung), wählen Sie diejenigen aus, die Sie tatsächlich gewinnen und profitabel bedienen können (Targeting), und entscheiden Sie sich dann für die eine Idee, die Sie in deren Köpfen besitzen möchten (Positionierung).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: Positionierung ist eine Entscheidung darüber, was Sie *nicht* sein werden.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: Eine Marke, die Premium, günstig, am schnellsten und am gesündesten ist, ist keines von alledem.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: Der Marketing-Mix – was werden wir tatsächlich tun?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: Die klassischen **4 Ps**: Produkt (was es ist, was es verspricht), Preis (was es kostet und was das signalisiert), Platzierung (wo und wie die Leute es bekommen können), Promotion (wie sie davon erfahren).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: Dienstleistungen fügen oft drei weitere Ps hinzu – Menschen, Prozess, physische Evidenz –, denn bei einem Haarschnitt oder einem Zahnarztbesuch *ist* das Erlebnis das Produkt.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: Der Test für einen guten Plan ist Kohärenz: Die vier Ps sollten alle dieselbe Geschichte erzählen.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: Budget und Kontrolle – was wird es kosten und woher wissen wir, dass es funktioniert hat?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: Geld, Zeitplan, Verantwortliche und die Kennzahlen, die Sie überprüfen werden.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: Der Kontrollschritt ist derjenige, den die Leute überspringen, und er ist derjenige, der Marketing von einem Kostenfaktor zu einer Disziplin macht.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: Pläne sind Hypothesen.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: Die Kontrolle ist das Experiment.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: Das ist das ganze Semester: die Situation erforschen, einen Kunden auswählen, ein kohärentes Angebot erstellen, bewusst ausgeben und ehrlich messen.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz

segments.src: **Q1.** Which of these is a properly written marketing objective?

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Die heutigen Begriffe

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **Marketingplan** – Ein schriftliches Dokument, das die Situation, die Ziele, den Zielkunden, die Marketingmaßnahmen, das Budget und die zur Beurteilung der Ergebnisse verwendeten Kennzahlen darlegt.

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5 Cs** – Eine Checkliste zur Situationsanalyse: Unternehmen, Kunden, Mitbewerber, Partner, Kontext.

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** – Segmentierung, Targeting, Positionierung: den Markt unterteilen, auswählen, wen man bedienen möchte, und die Idee definieren, die man in deren Köpfen besitzen möchte.

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **Marketing-Mix (4 Ps)** – Produkt, Preis, Platzierung, Promotion; die steuerbaren Hebel, die ein Unternehmen nutzt, um seine Positionierung zu erfüllen.

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC und LTV** – Kundengewinnungskosten im Vergleich zum Lifetime-Beitrag, den ein Kunde generiert; das Verhältnis zwischen ihnen sagt Ihnen, ob das Wachstum nachhaltig oder nur teuer ist.

vi.title: [Marketing 101 #15] Bài học cuối cùng: Tóm gọn cả một học kỳ vào một trang

segments.src: > A marketing plan is just five honest answers — where we are, who we're for, what we'll offer, what it costs, and how we'll know it worked — written down where everyone can see them.
segments.tr: > Một kế hoạch tiếp thị chỉ là năm câu trả lời trung thực — chúng ta đang ở đâu, chúng ta dành cho ai, chúng ta sẽ cung cấp những gì, chi phí là bao nhiêu và làm thế nào để biết nó hiệu quả — được viết ra ở nơi mà mọi người đều có thể nhìn thấy.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái niệm hôm nay

segments.src: Every marketing idea you've ever heard is trying to answer one question: **why would a stranger give you money instead of giving it to someone else?**
segments.tr: Mọi ý tưởng tiếp thị mà bạn từng nghe đều đang cố gắng trả lời một câu hỏi: **tại sao một người lạ lại đưa tiền cho bạn thay vì đưa cho người khác?**

segments.src: A marketing plan is the document that forces you to answer it out loud.
segments.tr: Kế hoạch tiếp thị là tài liệu buộc bạn phải trả lời câu hỏi đó một cách rõ ràng.

segments.src: Most of them follow the same skeleton, and each bone corresponds to something marketers study all semester:
segments.tr: Hầu hết chúng đều tuân theo cùng một khung sườn, và mỗi phần tương ứng với một thứ mà các nhà tiếp thị nghiên cứu trong suốt cả học kỳ:

segments.src: Situation analysis — where are we, really?**
segments.tr: Phân tích tình hình — chúng ta thực sự đang ở đâu?**

segments.src: The common shorthand is the **5 Cs**: Company (what we're actually good at), Customers (who buys and why), Competitors (who else solves this), Collaborators (distributors, retailers, agencies), and Context (economy, regulation, technology, culture).
segments.tr: Cách viết tắt phổ biến là **5 chữ C**: Company (Công ty - chúng ta thực sự giỏi việc gì), Customers (Khách hàng - ai mua và tại sao), Competitors (Đối thủ cạnh tranh - ai khác giải quyết vấn đề này), Collaborators (Cộng tác viên - nhà phân phối, nhà bán lẻ, đại lý) và Context (Bối cảnh - kinh tế, quy định, công nghệ, văn hóa).

segments.src: Many teams compress this into a SWOT — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats — but SWOT is a summary of research, not a substitute for it.
segments.tr: Nhiều nhóm nén điều này thành SWOT — điểm mạnh, điểm yếu, cơ hội, thách thức — nhưng SWOT là bản tóm tắt nghiên cứu, không phải là sự thay thế cho nghiên cứu.

segments.src: If your situation analysis has no numbers in it, it's a mood board.
segments.tr: Nếu phân tích tình hình của bạn không có con số nào trong đó, thì đó chỉ là một bảng tâm trạng (mood board).

segments.src: Objectives — what does winning look like?**
segments.tr: Mục tiêu — chiến thắng trông như thế nào?**

segments.src: "Grow awareness" is not an objective; it's a wish.
segments.tr: "Tăng nhận thức" không phải là một mục tiêu; đó là một điều ước.

segments.src: An objective has a number, a metric, and a deadline: *increase repeat purchase rate from 22% to 30% by Q4.* Vague goals are how marketing budgets quietly disappear.
segments.tr: Một mục tiêu phải có con số, chỉ số và thời hạn: *tăng tỷ lệ mua lại từ 22% lên 30% vào quý 4.* Những mục tiêu mơ hồ là cách ngân sách tiếp thị lặng lẽ biến mất.

segments.src: Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning (STP) — who is this for?**
segments.tr: Phân khúc, Nhắm mục tiêu, Định vị (STP) — điều này dành cho ai?**

segments.src: Split the market into groups that behave differently (segmentation), pick the ones you can actually win and serve profitably (targeting), then decide the one idea you want to own in their heads (positioning).
segments.tr: Chia thị trường thành các nhóm có hành vi khác nhau (phân khúc), chọn những nhóm bạn thực sự có thể chiến thắng và phục vụ một cách có lợi nhuận (nhắm mục tiêu), sau đó quyết định một ý tưởng duy nhất bạn muốn sở hữu trong tâm trí họ (định vị).

segments.src: Positioning is a choice about what you will *not* be.
segments.tr: Định vị là một lựa chọn về việc bạn sẽ *không* là gì.

segments.src: A brand that's premium, cheap, fastest, and healthiest is none of those things.
segments.tr: Một thương hiệu vừa cao cấp, vừa rẻ, vừa nhanh nhất, vừa lành mạnh nhất thì thực ra chẳng là gì cả.

segments.src: The marketing mix — what will we actually do?**
segments.tr: Hỗn hợp tiếp thị — chúng ta sẽ thực sự làm gì?**

segments.src: The classic **4 Ps**: Product (what it is, what it promises), Price (what it costs and what that signals), Place (where and how people can get it), Promotion (how they hear about it).
segments.tr: **4 chữ P** cổ điển: Product (Sản phẩm - nó là gì, nó hứa hẹn điều gì), Price (Giá cả - chi phí bao nhiêu và điều đó báo hiệu điều gì), Place (Địa điểm - mọi người có thể lấy nó ở đâu và như thế nào), Promotion (Xúc tiến - làm thế nào họ biết về nó).

segments.src: Services often add three more Ps — People, Process, Physical evidence — because in a haircut or a dentist visit, the experience *is* the product.
segments.tr: Các dịch vụ thường thêm ba chữ P nữa — People (Con người), Process (Quy trình), Physical evidence (Bằng chứng vật lý) — bởi vì khi cắt tóc hoặc đi nha sĩ, trải nghiệm *chính là* sản phẩm.

segments.src: The test of a good plan is coherence: the four Ps should all be telling the same story.
segments.tr: Bài kiểm tra của một kế hoạch tốt là sự mạch lạc: bốn chữ P đều phải kể cùng một câu chuyện.

segments.src: Budget and control — what will it cost, and how do we know it worked?**
segments.tr: Ngân sách và kiểm soát — chi phí là bao nhiêu và làm thế nào để biết nó hiệu quả?**

segments.src: Money, timeline, owners, and the metrics you'll check.
segments.tr: Tiền bạc, tiến độ, người chịu trách nhiệm và các chỉ số bạn sẽ kiểm tra.

segments.src: The control step is the one people skip, and it's the one that turns marketing from a cost center into a discipline.
segments.tr: Bước kiểm soát là bước mà mọi người thường bỏ qua, và đó là bước biến tiếp thị từ một trung tâm chi phí thành một kỷ luật.

segments.src: Plans are hypotheses.
segments.tr: Các kế hoạch là các giả thuyết.

segments.src: Control is the experiment.
segments.tr: Kiểm soát là thí nghiệm.

segments.src: That's the whole semester: research the situation, choose a customer, build a coherent offer, spend deliberately, and measure honestly.
segments.tr: Đó là toàn bộ học kỳ: nghiên cứu tình hình, chọn khách hàng, xây dựng một đề nghị mạch lạc, chi tiêu có chủ đích và đo lường một cách trung thực.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong cuộc sống hàng ngày

segments.src: Say you run **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, a small coffee brand in Austin.
segments.tr: Giả sử bạn điều hành **Barton Springs Cold Brew**, một thương hiệu cà phê nhỏ ở Austin.

segments.src: You sell online nationwide and sit on shelves in a dozen Central Texas grocery stores.
segments.tr: Bạn bán hàng trực tuyến trên toàn quốc và có mặt trên các kệ hàng tại hàng chục cửa hàng tạp hóa ở Trung Texas.

segments.src: Last quarter you did $40,000 in revenue.
segments.tr: Quý trước bạn đạt doanh thu 40.000 đô la.

segments.src: You want $60,000.
segments.tr: Bạn muốn đạt 60.000 đô la.

segments.src: Here's the plan on one page.
segments.tr: Đây là kế hoạch trên một trang.

segments.src: **Situation:** Cold brew is crowded, and big national brands own the grocery aisle.
segments.tr: **Tình hình:** Cà phê ủ lạnh (cold brew) rất đông đúc, và các thương hiệu quốc gia lớn chiếm lĩnh lối đi trong cửa hàng tạp hóa.

segments.src: But your repeat customers rave about one thing — it's low-acid, and people with sensitive stomachs can drink it black.
segments.tr: Nhưng khách hàng quay lại của bạn lại khen ngợi một điều — nó ít axit, và những người có dạ dày nhạy cảm có thể uống đen.

segments.src: Competitors are shouting "bold" and "extra caffeine."
segments.tr: Các đối thủ cạnh tranh đang hô hào "đậm đà" và "thêm caffeine."

segments.src: Nobody is shouting "gentle."
segments.tr: Không ai hô hào "nhẹ nhàng."

segments.src: **Objective:** Grow quarterly revenue from $40K to $60K by December 31, with at least 40% coming from repeat customers.
segments.tr: **Mục tiêu:** Tăng doanh thu hàng quý từ 40.000 đô la lên 60.000 đô la vào ngày 31 tháng 12, với ít nhất 40% đến từ khách hàng quay lại.

segments.src: **STP:** Skip the college-student energy-seekers — that's a price war you'll lose.
segments.tr: **STP:** Bỏ qua những sinh viên đại học tìm kiếm năng lượng — đó là cuộc chiến về giá mà bạn sẽ thua.

segments.src: Target 30–55 year-old daily coffee drinkers in Texas metros who've cut back on coffee because it upsets their stomach.
segments.tr: Nhắm mục tiêu vào những người uống cà phê hàng ngày từ 30–55 tuổi ở các đô thị Texas, những người đã cắt giảm cà phê vì nó làm họ khó chịu dạ dày.

segments.src: Position as *the cold brew you can drink every morning without regretting it.*
segments.tr: Định vị là *loại cà phê ủ lạnh bạn có thể uống mỗi sáng mà không phải hối tiếc.*

segments.src: **Marketing mix:** Product — put "low-acid, smooth on your stomach" on the front label, not buried on the back.
segments.tr: **Hỗn hợp tiếp thị:** Sản phẩm — ghi "ít axit, êm dịu cho dạ dày của bạn" trên nhãn trước, không phải giấu ở mặt sau.

segments.src: Price — hold at $32 for a 4-pack subscription; a discount would undercut the premium claim.
segments.tr: Giá cả — giữ ở mức 32 đô la cho gói đăng ký 4 sản phẩm; giảm giá sẽ làm suy yếu tuyên bố cao cấp.

segments.src: Place — double down on H-E-B stores in health-conscious ZIP codes rather than chasing national distribution you can't service.
segments.tr: Địa điểm — tập trung gấp đôi vào các cửa hàng H-E-B ở các mã bưu chính quan tâm đến sức khỏe thay vì theo đuổi phân phối toàn quốc mà bạn không thể phục vụ.

segments.src: Promotion — customer testimonials on Instagram and a partnership with two Austin running clubs.
segments.tr: Xúc tiến — lời chứng thực của khách hàng trên Instagram và hợp tác với hai câu lạc bộ chạy bộ ở Austin.

segments.src: **Budget and control:** $9,000 for the quarter.
segments.tr: **Ngân sách và kiểm soát:** 9.000 đô la cho quý.

segments.src: And here's the number that decides everything:
segments.tr: Và đây là con số quyết định mọi thứ:

segments.src: Average order value:        $32
segments.tr: Average order value:        $32

segments.src: Gross margin:               55%
segments.tr: Gross margin:               55%

segments.src: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60
segments.tr: Contribution per order:     $32 x 0.55 = $17.60

segments.src: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00
segments.tr: Customer acquisition cost:  $18.00

segments.src: Your first sale to a new customer **loses about 40 cents.** That is not automatically a failure — it's only a failure if they never come back.
segments.tr: Lần bán hàng đầu tiên của bạn cho một khách hàng mới **lỗ khoảng 40 xu.** Đó không tự động là một thất bại — nó chỉ là thất bại nếu họ không bao giờ quay lại.

segments.src: At an average of 2.5 orders per year, lifetime contribution is roughly `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, against $18 to acquire — about 2.4 to 1.
segments.tr: Với trung bình 2,5 đơn hàng mỗi năm, đóng góp trọn đời là khoảng `2.5 x $17.60 = $44`, so với 18 đô la để có được khách hàng — tỷ lệ khoảng 2,4 trên 1.

segments.src: The plan works *only* if retention holds.
segments.tr: Kế hoạch chỉ hoạt động *nếu* tỷ lệ giữ chân được duy trì.

segments.src: So the metric you watch weekly isn't impressions or likes.
segments.tr: Vì vậy, chỉ số bạn theo dõi hàng tuần không phải là lượt hiển thị hay lượt thích.

segments.src: It's second-order rate.
segments.tr: Đó là tỷ lệ mua lại lần thứ hai.

segments.src: That's what a marketing plan really does: it drags the assumption you were quietly relying on out into the open, where you can test it.
segments.tr: Đó là những gì một kế hoạch tiếp thị thực sự làm: nó lôi giả định mà bạn đang âm thầm dựa vào ra ngoài ánh sáng, nơi bạn có thể kiểm tra nó.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt ba dòng

segments.src: 1. A marketing plan is a chain — situation, objectives, STP, marketing mix, budget and control — and a weak link anywhere breaks the whole thing.
segments.tr: 1. Kế hoạch tiếp thị là một chuỗi — tình hình, mục tiêu, STP, hỗn hợp tiếp thị, ngân sách và kiểm soát — và một mắt xích yếu ở bất cứ đâu cũng sẽ phá vỡ toàn bộ.

segments.src: 2. Positioning means deciding what you won't be; the 4 Ps should all reinforce that single choice.
segments.tr: 2. Định vị có nghĩa là quyết định những gì bạn sẽ không trở thành; 4 chữ P đều phải củng cố lựa chọn duy nhất đó.

segments.src: 3. Write down the number your plan depends on, then measure it — an untested plan is just an opinion with a budget.
segments.tr: 3. Viết ra con số mà kế hoạch của bạn phụ thuộc vào, sau đó đo lường nó — một kế hoạch chưa được kiểm chứng chỉ là một ý kiến với một ngân sách.

segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Marketing plan** — A written document laying out the situation, objectives, target customer, marketing actions, budget, and the metrics used to judge results.
segments.tr: - **Kế hoạch tiếp thị** — Một tài liệu bằng văn bản trình bày tình hình, mục tiêu, khách hàng mục tiêu, các hành động tiếp thị, ngân sách và các chỉ số được sử dụng để đánh giá kết quả.

segments.src: - **5 Cs** — A situation-analysis checklist: Company, Customers, Competitors, Collaborators, Context.
segments.tr: - **5 chữ C** — Một danh sách kiểm tra phân tích tình hình: Công ty, Khách hàng, Đối thủ cạnh tranh, Cộng tác viên, Bối cảnh.

segments.src: - **STP** — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning: dividing the market, choosing whom to serve, and defining the idea you want to own in their minds.
segments.tr: - **STP** — Phân khúc, Nhắm mục tiêu, Định vị: chia thị trường, chọn người để phục vụ và xác định ý tưởng bạn muốn sở hữu trong tâm trí họ.

segments.src: - **Marketing mix (4 Ps)** — Product, Price, Place, Promotion; the controllable levers a company uses to deliver on its positioning.
segments.tr: - **Hỗn hợp tiếp thị (4 chữ P)** — Sản phẩm, Giá cả, Địa điểm, Xúc tiến; các đòn bẩy có thể kiểm soát mà một công ty sử dụng để thực hiện định vị của mình.

segments.src: - **CAC and LTV** — Customer acquisition cost versus the lifetime contribution a customer generates; the ratio between them tells you whether growth is sustainable or just expensive.
segments.tr: - **CAC và LTV** — Chi phí thu hút khách hàng so với đóng góp trọn đời mà một khách hàng tạo ra; tỷ lệ giữa chúng cho bạn biết liệu sự tăng trưởng là bền vững hay chỉ là đắt đỏ.

segments.src: If customers buy repeatedly, lifetime contribution can comfortably exceed acquisition cost, which is exactly the Barton Springs case — but the plan then lives or dies on retention.
